source.title: Reward expectation extinction restructures and degrades CA1 spatial maps through loss of a dopaminergic reward proximity signal

confidence_rationale: Direct, causal, cellular-resolution test of the exact mechanism MECH-232 asserts: a VTA-dopaminergic reward-proximity signal in CA1 that governs the fidelity/stability/over-representation of the reward map rather than writing an explicit positive-valence field. Bidirectional evidence (extinction removes it; optogenetic VTA-DA inhibition reproduces it). Confidence held below 0.9 by rodent-to-REE transfer and because the paper does not directly dissociate 'implicit representational-quality expansion' from an explicit valence gradient the way MECH-232's CRUX demands -- it shows the correlates, not the approach-behaviour dissociation.
failure_signatures: The paper measures encoding-side map quality (over-representation, remapping rate, trial-to-trial reliability) but does not test whether the DA-modulated representation drives approach behaviour in the absence of an explicit positive gradient -- so it supports the representational-expansion premise of MECH-232 without confirming the load-bearing 'this expansion IS the approach mechanism' claim.

Reward-proximity DA signal is a ramping, expectation-dependent scalar; a reader could interpret 'reward proximity' as itself a graded valence-like signal, blurring the very implicit-vs-explicit distinction MECH-232 rests on.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In mice, VTA dopaminergic axons in CA1 carry a reward-expectation-dependent ramping reward-proximity signal; this signal maintains place-cell over-representation of reward locations and map reliability. Extinguishing reward expectation, or optogenetically inhibiting VTA dopaminergic neurons, abolishes reward over-representation, increases place-field remapping, and reduces trial-to-trial reliability -- while the animal stays behaviourally engaged.
mapping.ree_translation: Directly instantiates MECH-232's core: dopamine at reward-relevant locations acts on the fidelity, stability, and density of hippocampal place representations (REE's DA-modulated RBF representational expansion, SD-024) rather than stamping an explicit positive-valence tag. Loss of the DA signal degrades map quality without erasing engagement -- exactly the dissociation REE relies on to argue approach-valence enters hippocampal terrain implicitly, through representational quality.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper establishes DA-controls-map-quality (the SD-024 substrate premise) but not the MECH-232 CRUX that this quality expansion, absent an explicit gradient, produces approach behaviour. It is strong support for the representational leg and silent on the behavioural-dissociation leg. Rodent 2-photon imaging in a virtual linear track; transfer to REE's abstract RBF terrain is by analogy of function, not mechanism.
mapping.source_context: Head-fixed mice, virtual-reality linear track, two-photon Ca2+ imaging of CA1 pyramidal cells + GCaMP imaging of VTA dopaminergic axons in CA1; optogenetic inhibition of VTA dopaminergic neurons.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality causal study in a strong venue with converging correlational + optogenetic evidence. Mapping fidelity high on the representational-expansion premise, lower on the approach-dissociation CRUX. Transfer risk moderate: rodent spatial navigation -> REE abstract hippocampal terrain.
